the airborne inoculum of L. maculan s spores in the UK and Poland is composed of both virulent and avirulent strains, and the frequencies of these strains are subject to fluctuations in time and space.

AvrLm alleles are not equally expressed in the air-borne propagules of L. maculan s, and that the frequencies of Avrlm1 and Avrlm6 alleles in the airborne inoculum of L. maculan s in the UK and Poland are not constant over time.

AvrLm genes are highly variable in the airborne inoculum of L. macu-lans and their frequencies are influenced by the cropping system, including the use of resistance-based cultivars, and by climatic factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the AvrL gene pool of L. maculan s in the UK and Poland is dynamic, with a strong influence of the host resistance deployed, and with the UK having higher AvrL gene diversity than the Polish region.

the frequencies of the two avirulence alleles in the air-borne spore inoculum of L. maculan are highly variable and that the ratio of AvrL1 and Avr6 alleles in the airborne inoculum is a function of the relative frequencies of Rlm1- and Rlm6-based resistance genes in the oilseed rape cultivars grown in the vicinity of the sampling sites.
the AvrL m1 and Avr L m6 alleles are not randomly distributed in airborne inoculum and their fluctuations are influenced by both host and environmental conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the frequencies of the two avirulence alleles, AvrLm 1 and Avr Lm6, fluctuate in L. macu-lans airborne inoculum in Poland and the UK in a manner that reflects the deployment of resistance genes in the host crop.
the AvrL1 allele is more prevalent in L. macuans spore populations in the UK than in Poland.
the frequencies of avirulence alleles of L. maculan in the airborne inoculum of this pathogen in Europe are highly variable and can be influenced by the cropping patterns of the host plant.
